conflicts.fact: Order of lessons covering Group 1 and Group 2 and which lesson showed sodium in water; the sequence's cross-references do not match
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 teaches alkaline earth metals and refers to alkali metals 'in Lesson 2'; Lesson 4 teaches alkali metals (with demos of Li/Na/K in water) and says it draws on 'Lesson 3' and bridges to Group 2 and Lesson 5; Lesson 6 teaches Group 2 again and refers to the sodium-in-water demonstration 'from Lesson 3'; Lesson 7 refers to sodium touching water in Lesson 2. Group 2 is taught twice (L3 and L6) and the sodium demo is placed in L2, L3 and L4.

Lesson 3 says it prepares for halogen investigations in Lesson 4; Lesson 4 is on alkali metals and Lesson 5 is noble gases. Lesson 5 says halogens and alkali metals were studied in Lessons 2-4 and refers to chlorine bleaching a flower, but no lesson in the sequence teaches halogens. Lesson 7 says it compares 'all four families studied so far' and Lesson 8 recalls hibiscus bleaching and iodine tests that never appear.

conflicts.fact: Noble gas outer electron count/group number
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 calls noble gases Group 0 whereas Lessons 5 and 8 call them Group 18; Lesson 5 research example row lists neon with 8 outer electrons while helium must have 2, yet Lesson 5 says all have 'completely full' shells and teacher says argon has 'eight outer electrons' (consistent), while Lesson 8 mentions helium with two. Also Lesson 5 says noble gases were already ask 'Lesson 4 sticky note' about stability though Lesson 4 is Group 1.

conflicts.fact: Why sodium glows in the street lamp / what happens to the electron; and sodium flame colour
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says sodium 'loses its single outer electron to produce the orange glow'; Lesson 4 says sodium doesn't react chemically in the lamp, electron is excited and re-emits light; Lesson 8 says sodium burns violet in water, while Lesson 4 says potassium (not sodium) gave the lilac/violet flame.

conflicts.fact: Why Group 2 is less reactive than Group 1 and reactivity explanation
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 explains reactivity by distance from nucleus/shielding down a group; Lesson 6 explains Group 2 being less reactive because the nucleus attracts two electrons 'more effectively' and it is harder to lose both, while Lesson 3 says removing two electrons takes more energy than one. Lesson 6 contradicts Lesson 3 by saying magnesium reacts slowly with cold water with a faint film, while Lesson 3 says no noticeable reaction with cold water.

conflicts.fact: Dilute HCl concentration and the magnesium-steam reaction rate
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 uses 0.5 M HCl and says reaction with steam was slower than with acid; Lesson 6 uses 1 mol/L HCl and describes steam reaction as moderate.
Lesson 3 says calcium and magnesium are used in CAN; Lesson 6 says calcium is the active ingredient. Lesson 6 ties CAN to Nakuru/Uasin Gishu.

conflicts.fact: Location of Kenyan welding and neon uses
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1-4 and 8 place the jua kali welder in Kamukunji; Lesson 5 places him on River Road, Nairobi (the Model Card still says Kamukunji).
Lesson 1 says the first-draft model will be redone at the end of Lesson 7 and the DQB updated over eight lessons; Lesson 8 is the final capstone model revision.
